sequential.note: MoviePy. Measured before the -t correctness fix, which did not touch this path.

finding.summary: 98% of the speedup is present before any parallelism. Replacing MoviePy with one direct ffmpeg per slide, still fully serial, is 12.64x on its own. Running those encodes concurrently adds a further 1.37x and saturates around 4 workers, because each ffmpeg is already multi-threaded. The bottleneck was the library, not the lack of parallelism.

correctness: Output verified at 417.56s against a 417.42s narration total and the original run's own video, identical at every pool width. An earlier version used -shortest and overran by ~2.9s per segment by a differing amount each run; it is now given an explicit -t.
